question_text: Why does the flag have 50 stars?

official_answers.text: (Because there is) one star for each state

why_it_matters.text: The flag's 50 stars represent the 50 states that make up the United States today. Unlike the stripes (fixed at 13 for the original colonies), the stars change every time a new state joins. The current 50-star flag has flown since July 4, 1960 — the year after Hawaii became the 50th state. It is the longest-serving version of the U.S. flag in history.

fun_fact.text: In 1958, 17-year-old Ohio high schooler Robert Heft designed a 50-star flag as a class project — when there were only 48 states! He predicted Alaska AND Hawaii would join. His teacher gave him a B-. Heft sent it to Washington. President Eisenhower picked his design as the official U.S. flag in 1960. The teacher changed the grade to an A.
